title: Quantization bias & regression benchmarking for FP8/INT8 profiles across batchers and long context
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, artifact-backed benchmarking pipeline to measure accuracy drift and latency/throughput regressions introduced by candidate FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles across different batcher behaviors and long-context workloads. We need to understand: (1) how calibration set composition affects per-layer scale factors and downstream generation quality, (2) interaction between continuous/dynamic batching and KV-cache warmup on tail latency for long contexts, and (3) where deterministic versus stochastic calibration methods produce divergent results that could cause customer-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark run that produces a single CSV summarizing token/sec, p50/p90/p99 latency, and perplexity/ROUGE/EM where applicable for each quant profile and batching mode
Calibration artifacts (scale tensors) for each profile stored and versioned in S3 with metadata linking to the exact code/seed
Regression detection: signal thresholds and a failing CI job that flags >3% quality drop or >15% latency regression on P90 compared to FP16 baseline
Dashboard with per-profile swimlanes showing throughput vs. sequence-length bucket and warm/cold KV-cache comparison
Runbook entry describing how to rerun calibration with a different seed or dataset and how to roll back a profile if deployed
test_plan: Models: run on r-infer-test-gpu with model variants 'gptx-7b' and 'gptx-13b' using FP16 baseline and candidate FP8 and INT8 profiles
Batching modes: static-batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16], dynamic-batcher with target latency SLOs (10ms, 25ms), and continuous-batching optimistic and conservative schedulers
Contexts: short (<=128), mid (512), long (2048, 4096) with a mixture of short+long prefix workloads to emulate real prompts
KV-cache: measure cold-start (first token) and warmed (after 64 tokens) conditions; capture p50/p90/p99 for both

Calibration variants: per-channel symmetric, per-tensor asymmetric, and a hybrid per-block approach; seeds [42, 1337, 2024]; calibration datasets: synthetic unigram set, internal prompt-mix 10k, public bookscorpus-sampled 5k
Quality metrics: next-token perplexity on held-out sets, BLEU/ROUGE on generation tasks, and a small human-eval surrogate score via existing eval harness
Stability checks: run each configuration 3x to compute variance and check for non-deterministic divergence
Resource measurements: GPU utilization, kernel timings (from nvtx traces), and per-token compute cost estimate
timeline: 2025-02-07: Kickoff and definition of acceptance criteria
2025-02-10: Implemented calibration runner and metadata manifest
2025-02-12: First full sweep on gptx-7b (static batches, FP8 profiles) — found a P90 regressions in dynamic-batcher
2025-02-17: Added warm/cold KV-cache splits and reproducibility seeds to pipeline
2025-02-20: Mid-sprint review; triage next actions and prioritize top failing profiles for remediation
decisions: Use three calibration seeds by default (42, 1337, 2024) and persist scales for each seed to assess stochastic calibration variance
Adopt per-channel symmetric scaling as the default candidate profile for INT8 because it produced the lowest average perplexity in early tests
Flag any profile with >3% relative BLEU/ROUGE drop or >15% P90 latency increase as a hard-fail in CI
Prefer storing raw calibration histograms in S3 to enable post-hoc re-calibration without re-running data collection
open_questions: What is the acceptable variance threshold for repeating calibration runs in CI (currently using 3 runs) before declaring a non-deterministic profile?
Should we expand synthetic calibration sets to include adversarial prompts to stress out activation distributions?
Do we need to coordinate with Dedicated capacity team to run larger multi-GPU throughput sweeps for INT8 kernels?
How to best present calibration provenance to customers when private deployments request reproducibility (which metadata fields are required)
